# Temple Scroll Column 54 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 54 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**54:1** Do not charge your fellow Israelite interest — whether on money, food, or anything else that is loaned.

**54:2** You may charge a foreigner interest, but not a fellow Israelite, so that the LORD your God will bless everything you do in the land you are about to enter and possess.

**54:3** When you make a promise to the LORD your God, do not put off fulfilling it, for the LORD your God will certainly hold you to it, and you will be guilty of sin.

**54:4** But if you choose not to make a vow, you will not be guilty.

**54:5** Whatever you freely promise with your own lips, you must make sure to carry out, just as you have voluntarily vowed to the LORD your God.

**54:6** If you enter your neighbor's vineyard, you may eat as many grapes as you want until you are satisfied, but do not carry any away in a basket.

**54:7** If you walk through your neighbor's grain field, you may pick some heads of grain by hand, but you must not harvest his grain with a sickle.

**54:8** If a man marries a woman and later becomes displeased with her because he finds something objectionable about her, he must write her a formal letter of divorce, give it to her, and send her away from his house.

**54:9** After she leaves his house, she may go and marry another man.

**54:10** If her second husband also turns against her and gives her a letter of divorce, or if the second husband dies —

**54:11** then her first husband, who divorced her, is not allowed to remarry her, since she has been defiled. That would be detestable to the LORD, and you must not bring guilt upon the land that the LORD your God is giving you as your inheritance.

**54:12** When a man has just married, he must not be sent out with the army or be given any other public responsibility. He shall be free to stay home for one year and bring happiness to the wife he has married.

**54:13** Do not take someone's millstone — or even just the upper stone — as collateral for a debt, because that would be taking away his means of survival.

**54:14** If anyone is caught kidnapping a fellow Israelite and treating him as a slave or selling him, the kidnapper must be put to death. In this way you shall root out the evil from among you.

**54:15** When an infectious skin disease breaks out, be very careful to follow exactly what the Levitical priests tell you to do. Follow the instructions I have given them.

**54:16** Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam while you were on the way out of Egypt.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 54 covers Deuteronomy 23:19-24:9. "Letter of divorce" for sefer keritut — accessible modern equivalent. "Something objectionable" for ervat davar — avoiding the overly literal "nakedness" language. "Means of survival" for "soul/life" in the millstone prohibition explains the underlying principle. "Infectious skin disease" for tsara'at conveys the medical quarantine context.*
